0.reason: answered by the repair round: one shared mutant harness (scripts/west_iron_galerkin/mutant.py, 03aa5258d) replaces both copies, guarded by duplication.py

findings.text: scripts/west_iron_galerkin/negative_asymmetry.py re-implements the mutant harness that scripts/west_iron_galerkin/negative.py:1 already owns — rev-parse, git archive of the same four paths, tar extract, in-place source mutation, identity assertion, pytest run and blob-versus-HEAD comparison are duplicated line for line rather than factored into a shared helper. It duplicates the owner rather than extending it, so one change to the extraction or the identity guard must be made twice.

The cell-interaction row of the parity table records a maximum relative difference of 0, and the run's parity.log header names parity-job.log as its arm log — but parity-job.log exited 1 with NameError: name 'np' is not defined before printing any PARITY line, and the PARITY record's gram_relative_frobenius field cannot be produced by the parity.py left on disk. The comparison was recomputed by an inline command whose only record is the run stream, so the headline no-behaviour-change number has no reproducible script or readable comparison log behind it.

The done_when requires the averaged external field on WEST's saved mesh unchanged to 1e-12, and the near-source probe differs by 0.199 relative (4.53e-7 T absolute). The fragment discloses this and reasons that a filament at r=0.05 m sits on the mesh boundary, so the integrand is not resolvable at fixed order — but the gate asserts only the uniform and smooth probes, so the clause as written is not met for one recorded input and the gate cannot fail on it.

The pre-symmetrisation asymmetry is asserted only on the 44-cell sphere (orders 8, 16, 24) and the 228-cell shell (orders 8, 16). The brief asked for the sweep on the WEST saved mesh as well, and the fragment records that mesh at order 4 only, outside the suite. The one mesh whose proximity to the production case matters most therefore has a single unasserted sample, so a regression that only shows at higher order there would not be caught.

changed_paths carries a shell redirect captured into the path: 'docs/figures/iron-core-magnetisation/icm-galerkin-interaction/spectrum-ramp 2>/dev/null' names no file that exists, and the same corruption appears in the orientation_write_paths line at line 3, which also omits docs/evidence/fragments/iron-core-magnetisation/icm-galerkin-cleanup.html and the two icm-galerkin-cleanup figure directories. A consumer that resolves changed_paths against the tree will not find the one figure the node actually changed. The manifest also carries no structured baseline_suite or after_suite block; both arms are recorded only as prose and as logs.
